## Overview
Document authenticity platform anchored on the Cardano blockchain. A microservices monorepo with 15+ backend services (API gateway, auth, originate, anchoring, timestamping, KYC, analytics, M365 integration, etc.) and three React frontends (Issuer Portal, Verifier Portal, Admin Dashboard).

Blockchain/Dev/
├── services/          # 15+ Node.js microservices (auth, originate, anchoring, etc.)
├── frontend/          # React apps: issuer/, verifier/, admin/
├── contracts/         # Aiken smart contracts (Cardano)
├── packages/          # Shared: validation (Zod), pagination, Redis cache, DB
├── migrations/        # Prisma/PostgreSQL migrations

├── systemTest/        # E2E + integration tests — has its own auto-loaded systemTest/CLAUDE.md (test standards)

```

## AI Behaviour Rules

**Package Manager**
- Always use `pip3`, never `pip` — applies to all install commands, scripts, and documentation

**Python Version**
- All Python code changes must target **Python 3.14+** — no exceptions
- Use Python 3.14+ syntax exclusively: `X | None` (not `Optional[X]`), `dict[K, V]` (not `Dict[K, V]`), `list[T]` (not `List[T]`), `tuple[A, B]` (not `Tuple[A, B]`)
- Do not add compatibility shims, `from __future__ import annotations`, or `typing_extensions` imports to work around 3.14 syntax
- **Check `python3 --version` before running or validating any Python code in the sandbox.** If it reports below 3.14 (e.g. 3.10), do not run/validate Python in-sandbox — tell the user to run quality gates locally in their 3.14 venv. If it reports 3.14+, in-sandbox runs are fine (subject to network access for dependency installs).

**Secrets — report the problem, never solve it**
- **Never open, read, quote or edit a secrets file in a session** — `.env`, `.env.local`,
  rendered `Docker.appsettings.*` configs, Key Vault / Secrets Manager output, or any
  restored local-secrets file. Reading one costs the team a full rotation of everything
  in it (this happened on platform-s PS-309, 2026-07-17).
- **When an issue involves secrets, report it and stop.** Name the file and the symptom,
  say which *key* to check and what shape its value should have, and let a person make
  the change. Naming a key is fine; seeing its value is not — no patch, no worked
  example, no "just set it to…".
- A diagnosis that dead-ends at that boundary is the correct outcome. Say so explicitly
  and hand the step over rather than looking.

**External repositories — never create a GitHub cross-reference (KS-1270 / KS-1271, 2026-09-18)**
- In anything GitHub renders as a commit message, PR title/body/review, issue or comment, refer
  to another organisation's issue or PR in **plain words only** (`upstream schemathesis issue
  4807`) — never a full `github.com/<owner>/<repo>/...` URL and never `owner/repo#N`. GitHub
  turns either into a public, undeletable cross-reference on the other repository naming this
  private one (it happened on PR #1047). `Secuura/…` links and links inside tracked files are fine.
- Applies to every repository and every commit/PR Claude writes, not only systemTest. The full
  rule, the incident and the pre-push grep live in `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` → *No links to other
  organisations' issues or PRs in git metadata (MUST)* — one canonical text; do not duplicate it.

**Scope discipline**
- Fix only what is explicitly requested — never infer extra tasks from hedging phrases like "may need", "could check", or "might want"
- When asked to "comply" with a standard: run the quality command, fix only what it flags, stop
- Do not fetch external URLs, changelogs, GitHub releases, or package registries unless the current message explicitly instructs it

## Document naming — systemTest folder

All Markdown documentation (`.md` files) created anywhere in the `systemTest/` folder and its
subfolders must follow **kebab-case naming convention**:

**Format:** `example-document-name.md`
- All lowercase letters
- Words separated by hyphens (`-`)
- No spaces, underscores, or camelCase
- No uppercase letters

**Examples (correct):** `getting-started.md`, `how-to-test-secuura.md`, `openapi-explorer.md`,
`test-data-management.md`, `error-handling-guide.md`

**Examples (incorrect — do NOT use):** `GettingStarted.md` (PascalCase), `getting_started.md`
(snake_case), `Getting Started.md` (spaces), `gettingStarted.md` (camelCase)

`README.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are the two exceptions, by universal convention — and renaming
`CLAUDE.md` would stop the tooling finding it.

**This is the single source for the rule (KS-682).** It previously existed twice and the two
copies contradicted each other: this file said kebab-case while `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` said
snake_case and listed `getting-started.md` as ❌. Fourteen files across six packages had been
named to the snake_case copy. Keep the rule here only; a second copy is how they diverged.

## Key Rules
- .env and .env.local are gitignored — never commit
- **Docker stack slots are a LOCAL-HOST mechanism only (MUST, 2026-09-14).** `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT`
  / `STACK_SLOT` (KS-666) select an isolated stack — ports offset by `100*(N-1)`, own compose
  project, volumes, network and `secuura-sN-*` container names — **for a build on the developer's
  local host and nothing else.** The slot number MUST NOT be applied to, or assumed by, any other
  related build: the VM demo (`demo-pk.secuura.net`, `/home/secuura/secuura/Dev`), the Azure
  Container Apps template, CI/pre-merge runs, or a teammate's machine. Those build and run
  unslotted — historic ports, historic names — and a slot number in their commands, env files,
  compose overrides or docs is a defect. Pass the slot on the command line of the local build
  (`SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=N ./Start_Up/start-secuura.sh …`, `STACK_SLOT=N npm test`); never bake it
  into anything that leaves the host.
- **Every slot value is CALCULATED from slot 1 (MUST, 2026-09-14).** Slot 1 holds the historic
  bases (gateway 6882, Postgres 6432, Redis 6379, tokenomics 8881, website 6881, prefix `secuura`,
  Compose's default project); slot N is derived from them — port `base + 100*(N-1)`, prefix
  `secuura-sN`, project `secuura_slotN` — in exactly one place, `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/stack_env.sh`
  (`systemTest/slot-target.sh` for the harnesses). Nothing else types a per-slot number: no
  `6982`/`7182`/`secuura-s2-…` literal in code, compose overrides, env files, tests or docs. Tests
  that assert a slot's ports or names compute the expectation from the slot-1 base too
  (`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/start_secuura_slot_names.test.sh` is the shape), so a wrong
  literal cannot pass against an equally wrong literal.
- Use `docker compose` (v2), NOT `docker-compose` (v1) — local dev is on Docker Desktop
- Cardano smart contracts are in Aiken (not Solidity)
- **Live tenant is the new Founders Hub tenant** `efc17e5f-7637-4118-b92c-c5236d591cad` (`philipcuffyahooco.onmicrosoft.com`), sub `a0ee7d32-...`. The OLD Secuura tenant `4012a4e8-26db-400b-b933-75f9931ed6e2` was **decommissioned + is dead (2026-06-25)**. Both differ from Datasec (kreiser.org Default Directory).

## Backend validation standards (services + packages)
- **Trim user-facing string fields (KS-202).** Every Zod schema for a free-text
  user input — name, title, description, reason, label, code, email, org/domain,
  phone — must call `.trim()`, and `.trim()` must come **before** `.min()`,
  `.max()`, `.email()`, or any content check so the constraint applies to the
  trimmed value (`z.string().trim().min(1)` rejects `'   '`; `.min(1).trim()`
  does not). Compose from the shared bases (`@secuura/shared` `emailSchema`/
  `nonEmptyStringSchema`; `services/shared` `SafeStringSchema`/`EmailSchema`) so
  the fix propagates. **Do NOT trim** passwords, tokens, hashes, API keys,
  Base64 payloads, or free-form `metadata` values — trimming corrupts those.
- **Keep base string schemas chainable.** Express content checks on a base
  string schema with `.regex()` (returns `ZodString`, still `.min()/.max()`-able),
  not `.refine()` (returns `ZodEffects`, which has no `.min()/.max()` and throws
  "min is not a function" at module load if a derived schema chains them).

## Branching — Git Flow (adopted 2026-05-25, KS-137)
`main` = stability/production (always releasable; only `release/*` + `hotfix/*` merge here).
`develop` = integration; `feature/*` branch from and merge into `develop`; `release/*` and
`hotfix/*` fold back into both. Use Linear's suggested `gitBranchName` for ticketed work.
Nothing reaches `main`/`release/*` without the pre-merge gate green (KS-105).
Full model: **`Blockchain/Dev/CONTRIBUTING.md` → Branching Model**.

**Pull-request rules (always):**
- **Every PR summary/description MUST include the Linear ticket URL** (e.g.
  `https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-390`). When opening or updating a PR, put the
  ticket link in the summary so the PR ↔ ticket link is one click away.
- **Before merging a PR, the pre-merge suites MUST be run and pass, and the author
  acknowledges it in the PR description.** The pre-merge tiers are the Schemathesis
  sweep (`pre-merge-platform-suites.yml` → `run.py pre-merge`) and the Akto scan
  (`npm run test:pre-merge`); the workflow is `workflow_dispatch`-disabled, so trigger
  it manually (or run the two suites locally) and confirm green — the fast PR gate
  alone is not sufficient. **The PR template (`.github/pull_request_template.md`)
  seeds two author-acknowledgment checkboxes (Schemathesis, Akto) + a Linear line**,
  and **`.github/workflows/pr-premerge-ack.yml`** enforces them with three checks —
  **`Pre-merge acknowledged — Schemathesis`**, **`Pre-merge acknowledged — Akto`**,
  **`Linear ticket present`** (drafts exempt). **Built OFF by default:** while the repo
  Variable `ENFORCE_PREMERGE_ACK` is unset, a missing box/ticket only **warns** and the
  check still **passes green** (so nothing shows red before it's turned on). To enforce:
  (1) set `ENFORCE_PREMERGE_ACK=true` (`gh variable set ENFORCE_PREMERGE_ACK --body true`)
  so a missing box/ticket fails the check, then (2) add the check names to the develop AND
  main `require-pr-gates` rulesets and turn on required reviews = 1 (any writer). *[NOT APPLIED (2026-09-11, KS-1095): Kam has
  ruled on the required-approvals setting and that ruling is not yet applied; turning required reviews on
  while fleet PRs carry 0 GitHub reviews would block every fleet merge.]* The former
  Environment-based sign-off jobs were removed in favour of this checkbox approach.

## Pre-push preflight (KS-380) — run before pushing a feature branch
Before pushing platform (services/frontends/spec/deps) changes, run
`bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh` and clear anything it flags. It
runs the cheap cross-cutting sweeps the per-package gates miss — the mistakes
recent builds leaked to review: **OpenAPI spec drift** (`check:openapi`),
**lockfile clean-room** (`npm ci --dry-run` per standalone lock — KS-374/376/#399),
**spec-auth conformance** (every bearer-authed operation must 401/403 when
called unauthenticated — the KS-375 class; needs the local stack up on :6882),
**path resolvability** (every published op must route — AUTHED probe, fails
on the gateway's "Route … not found" 404; the KS-473 class the unauth sweep
can't see. Known-unroutable exceptions go in the script's `KNOWN_UNROUTABLE`
with a ticket ref, and come out when the ticket resolves), and the
**npm-audit gate** (KS-470 — ambient `npm audit` output is OFF in .npmrc; a
new or lapsed advisory outside the triaged
`scripts/audit/audit-baseline.json` fails, `npm run audit:gate` to run it
alone; baseline entries need a reason + ticket, temporary ones an `expires`),
and the **standalone-lock audit** (KS-531 — the npm-audit gate resolves the
HOISTED workspace tree, which dedupes away versions a service's own lock still
pins and ships in its image, so `npm run audit:locks` reads the lockfiles
directly and matches their pins against the registry's advisory data, sharing
the same baseline. The corpus is DERIVED, not typed: every tracked
`package-lock.json` (`git ls-files '*package-lock.json'` — 45 at develop
e02e15811), minus the `Blockchain/Dev` workspace root that `audit:gate`
covers, minus whatever is enumerated in `OUT_OF_SCOPE_LOCKS` — 43 scanned
today. The old figure of 35 was the count a four-directory walk under
`Blockchain/Dev` could see; it could not reach `systemTest/` or
`connectors/` at any depth, and the gate now prints the number with the
command that reproduces it rather than a constant that goes stale. Note: `npm audit` run *inside* a workspace member does NOT
read that member's lock — it audits the hoisted tree, which is why this reads
the lockfiles itself; see the header of `scripts/audit/audit-locks.mjs`).
It's additive to `npm test`/systemTest, not a replacement.
**Running the preflight from a `git worktree`? `npm ci` in it once first (KS-691).**
`node_modules` is gitignored and the root lock places ~218 deps in *nested* trees,
so a fresh worktree has none. Nothing-installed is reported honestly (KS-469); the
*partial* state — root present, nested absent — used to be announced as "spec
drifted" and is now caught by `scripts/preflight/deps-present.sh`. The standalone
`scripts/preflight` and `scripts/audit` members install themselves on first run.
Spec-only changes still have a live surface: the **api-gateway image bundles
`docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`** (served at `/api/docs` + the raw
`.yaml`/`.json` routes, and driving the gateway's spec-auth gate + 405 map).
**How to pick that change up differs by target — and the local case is NOT a
rebuild (corrected 2026-08-19, Kamil's KS-256 review §9):**
- **Deployed targets** (Container Apps / the VM's built images) — the spec is
  baked in, so **rebuild api-gateway**.
- **Local compose** — the spec is **bind-mounted**, not baked
  (the `secuura-api.yaml:/app/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml:ro` line in
  `docker-compose.yml`), and since KS-656 the gateway reads it into memory
  **once at boot** (`openApiSpecRaw = readFileSync(specPath, …)` in
  `api-gateway/src/index.ts`) so every spec surface has one source. So **`docker restart secuura-api-gateway`** is what
  picks up a regenerated spec. A rebuild also works, but only incidentally —
  it recreates the container, which re-boots it — so citing "the image bundles
  the spec" as the *reason* locally is wrong and sends people on a 10-minute
  rebuild for a 2-second restart.
- **Verify by checksum, because the failure mode is silent.** There *is* a
  dev-only `fs.watch` hot-reload, and whether it fires **depends on how the spec
  was written** — an in-place rewrite (what `npm run generate-openapi` does) is
  picked up; a replacement (`mv`, `rsync`, an image rebuild) is not.
  **`api-gateway/src/index.ts` is the authority on that split — read the comment
  above `fsWatch(specPath, …)` rather than trusting a restatement here** (measured
  by Peter 2026-08-31; KS-659 tracks making the reload unconditional). Restarting is
  still the reliable move, because it works for both write shapes. Worse, after a
  `git checkout` the single-file bind mount keeps pointing at the **dead inode**
  the old file had: the container path becomes unreadable while
  `/api/docs/openapi.yaml` keeps answering **200 with the previous branch's
  spec**. Kamil hit exactly this — 1,152,555 bytes served against the branch's
  1,232,278. So compare `md5sum` of the served bytes against the host file
  rather than trusting a 200. **If the checksums differ the mount is dead, and a
  restart will NOT clear it** — a bind resolves at container *create*, so the fix
  is `docker compose -f docker-compose.local.yml up -d --force-recreate --no-deps
  api-gateway`. (Measured again 2026-09-02: after checking out a branch whose
  spec differs, `md5sum` inside the container answered *"No such file or
  directory"*; one `--force-recreate` and host and container agreed, healthy in
  ~6 s.)

The swagger mount lives in `api-gateway/src/index.ts` (a dead root-level
`swagger.ts` duplicate was deleted 2026-07-17 — #553/#554).

## Date/time standards — UTC everywhere (KS-201)
Every timestamp is a legally-significant artefact (on-chain anchoring, audit,
eIDAS/UETA), so date/time handling must be unambiguous and region-independent.
- **Containers run `TZ=UTC`.** Set on every backend service in
  `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` and in the Azure bicep `commonEnvVars`
  (`deployment/azure/services.bicep`). Add it for any new service.
- **Don't rely on local-time Date methods or local-time date-fns.** Use
  `getUTCFullYear()/getUTCMonth()/getUTCDate()` (not `getFullYear()/getMonth()`),
  and UTC-explicit boundaries (`services/analytics/src/utils/utcDate.ts`:
  `startOfUtcDay`/`endOfUtcDay`/`startOfUtcMonth`/`endOfUtcMonth`) rather than
  date-fns `startOfDay`/`endOfMonth`, which operate in the process TZ.
- **Persisted/on-chain date strings must be deterministic.** Never build an
  NFT/VC/anchor date with `toLocaleDateString`/`toLocaleString` (locale + TZ
  dependent, and on-chain data is immutable) — format from UTC getters with
  fixed month names. UI-only display formatting may still use `toLocale*`.
- API responses keep `.toISOString()`; Postgres/Prisma already store `Date` as UTC.
